- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.20) — model tends to overshoot early in upward trends.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (negative sentiment < -0.30) — model fails to capture sharp declines or mean reversion.
- Lag in price corrections: model often delays downward adjustments after negative sentiment spikes.
- Overshoot after sharp upward moves: model overreacts to sentiment spikes, leading to inflated peaks.
- Mean reversion bias: model underestimates the strength of mean reversion in medium-term (15-30d) horizons, especially after strong rallies.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment > 0.30, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence; if sentiment < -0.30, increase forecast by 5–10% to compensate for underreaction.
